name: Dentures
title: Dentures in Edmonton, Cairns | South Cairns Dental
description: New dentures, replacements for old or loose dentures, and implant-retained dentures. Talk to South Cairns Dental in Edmonton about replacing missing teeth.

hero.title: Dentures
hero.lead: Whether it’s your first set or your old ones have stopped fitting, we’ll talk through the tooth replacement options that suit you.

intro.heading: Types of dentures
intro.html:
Full dentures replace all the teeth in the upper or lower jaw. Partial dentures fill gaps where some natural teeth remain, often clipping onto them for support. Implant-retained dentures attach to dental implants for a more secure fit.

Getting dentures usually takes several appointments, so they can be measured, tried in and adjusted until they look and feel right.

callout.title: Broken or lost your dentures?
callout.html: Call us. We treat broken and lost dentures as an urgent problem. Please don’t try to glue them yourself, and bring all the pieces with you.

items.title: Old or loose dentures
items.text: Dentures that rub, rock or slip can make eating and talking a chore. Your mouth changes over time, so a set that once fitted well may not now. We’ll check them and discuss your options.

items.title: Dentures for the first time
items.text: If you’re missing several teeth, or teeth may need to be removed, we’ll explain what dentures involve and how they compare with other choices.

items.title: Implant-retained dentures
items.text: Dentures can clip onto dental implants for a more secure fit. Ask whether this could suit you.

weigh.heading: Benefits and things to consider
benefits: Replace several or all missing teeth
Help with chewing, speech and appearance
Can usually be adjusted or relined as your mouth changes
consider: It takes time to get used to new dentures
The gums and jaw change shape over time, so the fit changes too
Loose dentures can cause sore spots
alternatives: A bridge for one or two missing teeth

care.heading: Looking after your dentures
items: Clean your dentures with a soft brush and a cleaner recommended by your dentist. Toothpaste can be too abrasive.
Your dentist may recommend taking dentures out at night to rest your gums. Keep them in water so they don’t dry out.
Brush your gums, tongue and any natural teeth too.
Keep having regular check-ups, even with a full denture, so your dentist can check the fit and the health of your mouth.

faqs: My dentures feel loose. What can I do?
Book a check. Your dentures may need adjusting, relining or replacing, or implant-retained dentures may be worth discussing.
How long until new dentures feel normal?
Everyone is different. It can take a few weeks to get used to eating and speaking. Come back if sore spots develop, as adjustments can help.
cost: The cost depends on what your mouth needs, so it can only be worked out after an examination.
